move: layer frames fly in and collapse into tile, brush stroke paints letters
how: Three translucent bordered rounded squares (layers) fly in from top-left (x:-420, rotation -18), top-right (x:420, rotation 14) and below (y:300) with move over the first 26%, staggered 0.12, then each scales down from 1.35/1.22/1.1 to 1 with expo.inOut at 22-37% so they stack into one. The solid Photoshop-blue tile fades and scales in from 0.9 at 30% while the layer frames fade out. Inside the tile a 'Ps' text is masked by a zig-zag path with a 90px-wide round-capped white stroke; the stroke draws with DrawSVG 0 to 100% (power2.inOut, 1.1s) from 36% so the letters appear painted on by three horizontal brush passes. Three colour swatches pop in scale 0/rotation 90 with back.out(2) (stagger 0.12) at 42% and bob y:-14 yoyo on sine.inOut. Exit at 87%: swatches shrink with back.in(2), the tile scales to 0.7 and fades.
adapt: Change the letters in the masked text, tile colour (#001e36), accent (#31a8ff) and swatch colours/positions; keep the three-direction layer arrival with its scale collapse and the 1.1s brush reveal. The zig-zag mask path must cover the text bounds.
port: mount(el, shot) inserts the layer frames, the tile with mask-defs SVG and the swatches; animate(el, shot, D) returns the same timeline with layers at 0-0.37 of D, brush at 0.36-0.64, exit at 0.87. Requires DrawSVGPlugin; the mask id must be unique per instance; swatch positions are absolute stage pixels and should be relative to el.
caveats: SVG mask id 'm' collides across instances
swatch positions are hard-coded stage pixel coordinates
stylised Ps tile, not the official Adobe mark
